recent_video_titles: Nobody talks about this part of practice… “Practice changes over time. Not always in visible ways. Not always in ways we can measure. But when we keep showing up – with consistency, with attention – the practice has its own way of changing us, even without us trying to control or force it. Something shifts. The way we move, listen, and stay. Not just on the mat, but in how we meet ourselves in moments that ask for presence. What once felt demanding becomes more familiar. What once required effort becomes more integrated. Growth in practice is rarely loud. It happens in small returns. In quiet consistency. In the willingness to keep showing up without needing immediate results. And over time, the practice stops being something we do – and becomes something we carry with us.” Sending our love and gratitude to Liforme Ambassador @svenja.yoga for sharing her real practice – flow, footprints and all the fierce and fabulous that comes with it – on her personalised Liforme Mindful Garden Yoga mat. 🙏❤️

Setting up for a Headstand 🙃 Inversions aren’t just about strength, they’re about technique too. Liforme Ambassador Christine Sit shares how she builds a stable headstand foundation: “This is how I set up my headstand base. I like pressing my wrists into the back of my head to create resistance as I shift my hips back and find balance. Do you set up like this too, or do you use a different method? I’d love to hear how you practice – share below! 👇☺️” Huge thanks to @christine_sit for this brilliant inversion guidance on her Liforme Cosmic Moon Yoga mat! ✨ #handstands

This time, it’s personal. 🖤🌙 Get a Yoga mat that suits you to a tee with Liforme X You, our mat customiser. “I loved being part of every detail, starting from the base colour. I knew I wanted something neutral, something black that could easily go with everything I wear. A foundation that feels simple, clean, and versatile. Choosing the accents, I was drawn to earthy shades – warm oranges and grounded tones that softly stand out against the black. There’s something about that contrast that feels both strong and natural at the same time. What I love the most is having “Liforme x Karlita” on the mat. That detail means so much to me – it makes it feel truly mine.” -Karlita Armenta ✨ Ready to create a mat that’s uniquely yours? Start designing via the link in our bio. Inspired by Karlita’s design? When your mat carries you home. 🧘‍♂️✨ Thanks to our dear friend, @movewitheli for taking us on a little trip… “As a Roman living abroad, the Tantalising Terracotta brings me back to the roots of my people. Its warm, earthy tones echo the clay tiles, sunlit rooftops, and ancient walls of Rome. Even from afar, it transports me home. The colours echo those of traditional mosaics, the careful placement of each piece creating something harmonious and whole. I’ve been thinking a lot about the little moments lately — the ones that used to send me into a full spiral, and how different they feel now. 🌀 Last month my car battery died on a day where everything already felt heavy. A year ago, that would’ve been the final straw. I would’ve shut down, cried, maybe canceled the whole day. But instead… I took a deep breath. And I actually let out a little giggle. 😅 Because in that moment I realized: life is always going to hand me things I can’t control, but I can control how I meet them. Last week I was running on fumes — work, a wedding & baby shower, the holidays, nonstop plans. Normally, that level of chaos would’ve left me feeling ungrounded. But when I finally sat down, I took a deep breath and thought: I just celebrated so much love. I get to reset. I get to be with family. What a gift.✨ And yesterday, when I was rushing out the door to my third job of the day, I felt that old familiar stress creeping in. But again… breathe. I remembered that I’m doing things I love. I remembered that this version of me once prayed to be here — building something, helping people, following my passions. 💖 I’m not perfect. I still get overwhelmed. I still catch myself slipping into old patterns. But every time I pause… every time I breathe… every time I choose presence over panic… I’m reminded that my life is unfolding in ways I never thought possible. 🌱 If you’re reading this: You’re allowed to slow down. 🐢 You’re allowed to take a breath before the spiral hits. 🧘🏼‍♀️ You’re allowed to choose peace even when life feels messy. And somehow… everything feels a little lighter when you do. 🤍✨

Whip up this one-pan meals with @Krista Torres 🍽️ grab the pan at our link in bio!  INGREDIENTS: 3 TBSP olive oil 1 finely diced onion 20 ounces potato gnocchi 1 1/4 cup cherry tomatoes, diced 2 TBSP tomato paste 1/3 cup heavy cream 4 garlic cloves, minced 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes 2-4 burrata cheese balls (cashew cheese can be substituted for vegan) Fresh basil as desired salt + pepper RECIPE Heat up your large skillet or Goodful deep cooker, pour in olive oil and swirl until it coats the bottom of the pan. Add in diced onions and garlic. Saute on medium heat until caramelized. In a separate pot, bring water to a boil and add in gnocchi. While the gnocchi is cooking, add cherry tomatoes, tomato paste, heavy cream, red pepper, salt, and pepper to the onions and garlic. Let them cook, occasionally stirring, for about 10-15 minutes or until the tomatoes are soft. When the gnocchi is done, drain it and add it the rest of the ingredients in the skillet. Complete the recipe by adding the burrata cheese and fresh basil. Enjoy!

Cauliflower Potato Soup Recipe:  INGREDIENTS: 🥔 Half a yellow onion, diced 🥔 1 TBSP olive oil 🥔 1 head of cauliflower, chopped 🥔 1 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cubed 🥔 3 cups chicken broth (or vegetable broth) 🥔 1 TBSP butter 🥔 1 cup heavy whipping cream 🥔 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese 🥔 1/2 cup chopped green onions 🥔 1 tsp smoked paprika 🥔 salt + pepper to taste RECIPE: 1. Heat olive oil in large pot over medium heat and add in chopped onions, sautéing for 5 minutes. 2. Add in cubed potatoes, chopped cauliflower, and broth. Turn up to high heat until it boils, then reduce to medium and cover for 25 minutes or until both potatoes and cauliflower are fully cooked. 3. Add in heavy whipping cream and pour mixture into a blender, blending until ingredients are smooth. 4. Pour mixture back into pot over low heat, adding in butter, seasonings and shredded cheese. Once melted, serve garnished with green onion.

Antes da sua primeira aula de yoga, tem algumas coisas simples, mas importantes, que fazem toda a diferença na experiência ✨ 🧘‍♀️ Roupa confortável Que permita alongar, sentar, torcer, se mover livremente. 👣 Prática é descalça Sem meia, sem sapato. Contato direto com o chão. 💛 Coração aberto Yoga não é só postura. É presença. 💦 Garrafinha de água Especialmente nas práticas mais intensas. 🧴 Toalhinha (Power Yoga) A gente sua. E tudo bem. Ela ajuda muito no conforto. 🧶 Cabelo preso / buchinha Parece detalhe, mas faz diferença no movimento e na concentração. 🧘‍♂️ Tapetinho de yoga Talvez o item mais importante. Ele ajuda na constância, na autonomia e no cuidado com o corpo. E sim: levar o seu tapete também faz parte do respeito com o espaço 🌱 Yoga começa antes da postura. Começa na forma como você chega. Se você sente que é o momento de cuidar de si com mais consciência, me conta aqui nos comentários: ✨ você já pratica yoga ou seria sua primeira vez?

O início de um novo ciclo não pede pressa. Pede presença. Janeiro é esse espaço entre o que ficou para trás e o que ainda não foi escolhido. É o momento de parar, respirar e se perguntar com honestidade: isso que eu estou vivendo é o meu caminho… ou o caminho que eu aprendi a seguir? O corpo sempre responde antes da mente. Ele pesa quando algo não é verdadeiro. Ele expande quando estamos alinhados. Mas pra escutar, é preciso silenciar o ruído. E pra decidir, é preciso sentir. Por isso, nesses primeiros dias de 2026, o convite é simples — mas profundo: escute antes de agir. No nosso canal, você encontra práticas, meditações e conversas pra desacelerar, observar o que o corpo sente e reconhecer com mais clareza o que faz sentido continuar — e o que não faz mais. Porque transformação não nasce só da reflexão. Ela nasce quando a escuta encontra a ação consciente. Se algo dentro de você está pedindo ajuste, direção ou verdade… talvez esse seja o chamado. 🌱 Vem comigo viver esse mês. Ogni volta che sali sul tappetino, non stai solo muovendo il corpo.  Stai ascoltando.  Stai osservando dove sei rigido e dove sei sciolto, dove resisti e dove ti arrendi.  Ti stai conoscendo attraverso l'unico strumento che hai sempre con te: te stesso. Non serve cercare risposte fuori. Non serve imitare la posizione perfetta di qualcun altro. Lo yoga non ti chiede di diventare qualcun altro. Non ti chiede di raggiungere una versione ideale di te. Ti chiede semplicemente di guardarti, ascoltarti, conoscerti. E lo fai attraverso il corpo. Attraverso il respiro. Attraverso ciò che hai già. Ogni pratica è un'opportunità per conoscerti meglio. Per scoprire qualcosa di nuovo su di te. O per ritrovare qualcosa che avevi dimenticato. Non serve andare lontano per trovare risposte. Tutto ciò che cerchi è già lì, sul tappetino, dentro di te. Il tappetino è uno specchio.  Quello che incontri lì – la pazienza, la fretta, la gioia, la frustrazione – è esattamente ciò che incontri nella vita. E questa è la magia: praticando, cambi.  Non perché qualcuno ti ha detto come devi essere, ma perché hai iniziato a vederti davvero. E tu, cosa stai scoprendo di te sul tappetino? 🙏

La cura di sé non è egoismo.  È il carburante che ti permette di brillare intensamente. Per troppo tempo abbiamo imparato a mettere gli altri prima di noi, a sentirci in colpa per ogni momento dedicato al nostro benessere. Ma la verità è questa: quando ti prendi cura di te, non sottrai nulla a nessuno. Anzi. Crei spazio per dare di più, con più presenza, più energia, più amore. Perché quando ti svuoti, quando ti consumi, non hai più nulla da dare. Né a te, né agli altri. Il tappetino è il luogo dove ricordi che la tua felicità conta. Che tu meriti di brillare intensamente. Fai della tua felicità una priorità.

Quanto spesso ti metti per ultimo nella tua lista di priorità? Tra lavoro, famiglia, impegni... ti dimentichi di te. Ma prenderti cura di te non è egoismo. È necessario. Oggi fai quel piccolo passo che rimandi da troppo tempo. Anche tu conti. 💛 #yogaacademy

Ognuno di noi è qui per compiere il proprio dharma: un cammino unico, personale, irripetibile. Non quello che appare più facile, più giusto o più “perfetto” agli occhi degli altri. Il dharma è la tua verità interiore, la tua via. A volte potresti inciampare, sentirti incerto, non pronto. Ma ogni passo, anche imperfetto, ti avvicina alla tua vera natura. Vivere secondo il proprio dharma significa accogliere l’imperfezione, lasciare andare il confronto e ascoltare la voce più autentica che hai: quella dell’anima. Quando segui il tuo dharma, anche i passi incerti trovano senso. Gli errori diventano maestri. Ogni scelta fatta con verità è un atto di libertà. Non serve che sia perfetto. Serve solo che sia tuo. 💬 Ti sei mai chiesto se stai vivendo secondo il tuo dharma o quello che gli altri si aspettano da te?

Rafforza le gambe. Libera il bacino. Trova l'equilibrio dentro e fuori dal tappetino. Questo mini flow lavora su tre aspetti fondamentali: Rafforza le gambe per sostenere il corpo con stabilità Libera il bacino per permettere all'energia di fluire Migliora l’equilibrio per coltivare presenza e concentrazione. Questa sequenza è perfetta per alleviare lo stress e imparare a rimanere centrato anche quando tutto intorno vacilla. Sul tappetino e nella vita. ☺️ Salva questo flow e provalo quando hai bisogno di ritrovare il tuo centro. #yogaacademy #flow

Gli Yoga Sutra ci ricordano qualcosa di molto importante e che troppo spesso dimentichiamo: la pace non arriva quando otteniamo ciò che vogliamo, arriva quando smettiamo di mettere condizioni alla nostra serenità. Essere luminosi non significa essere perfetti.  Significa essere autentici.  Coerenti tra dentro e fuori.  Liberi dal peso delle maschere. E tutto questo inizia con un solo atto di coraggio: conoscersi davvero.  Guardarsi dentro senza giudizio.  Scoprire chi siamo al di là dei ruoli, delle aspettative, delle paure. Lo Yoga non impone nulla.  Propone. Propone un modo diverso di stare al mondo, in cui la felicità non dipende dalle circostanze ma dalla chiarezza con cui scegliamo di vivere ogni momento. Sul tappetino come nella vita. 💭 E tu, cosa stai aspettando per permetterti di essere in pace?

Yoga Mobility Routine Il tuo corpo ha bisogno di muoversi in tutte le direzioni. Questa sequenza di mobility ti aiuta a: Sciogliere le tensioni accumulate Migliorare la flessibilità senza sforzo Ritrovare libertà di movimento nelle articolazioni Preparare il corpo alla pratica (o alla giornata) Bastano pochissimi minuti. Salva questo reel e prova oggi. 💜 #yogamobility #yogaacademy #benessere #routine #movimentoconsapevole

Hai presente quella sensazione prima di sollevarsi completamente nelle posizioni di equilibrio sulle braccia? Un misto di paura, entusiasmo, concentrazione... E poi il momento in cui ti sollevi da terra tutto cambia! Le posture di equilibrio sulle braccia non sono solo una questione di forza fisica. Sono anche una pratica di fiducia e ascolto, gioco e leggerezza. Ogni caduta è parte dell’equilibrio. Ogni tentativo è un passo verso la libertà. 👉 Scopri i corsi dedicati a queste pratiche nella nostra scuola: link in bio! #yogaacademy

La pratica non è un esame. Non è una gara contro te stesso. Non è una scalata verso la perfezione. La pratica è uno spazio dove tornare. Pensiamo sempre che lo yoga sia un percorso verso un traguardo: la posizione perfetta, il corpo più flessibile, il respiro profondo. Ma la verità è che la perfezione è un'illusione che ci allontana da ciò che conta davvero. Ciò che conta è essere lì, sul tappetino. Respirare con il corpo che hai oggi. Muoverti con l'energia che senti oggi. Accogliere la mente così com'è, senza giudizio. La pratica è l'unico luogo dove non devi dimostrare niente. Non serve essere bravi, non serve essere all'altezza. Serve solo esserci. Nel momento presente. Così come sei. Ogni volta che stendi il tappetino, non stai cercando di conquistare qualcosa. Non stai inseguendo un risultato. Stai scegliendo di tornare a te. #yogaacademy #yogaquotes

First, let's talk about the ingredients. The key to this smoothie is the combination of fat-burning properties of these ingredients. Ginger is another great ingredient that has thermogenic properties that help to increase body temperature and burn fat. Lastly, cucumber is a low-calorie food that helps to detoxify the body and promote weight loss. Here's how to make the smoothie: 1. Gently peel and slice the kiwi. 2. Peel and slice the apple into small pieces. 3. Cut the ginger into thin pieces. 4. Remove the seeds and slice the cucumber. 5. Add all the ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth. 6. Pour the smoothie into a glass and add some ice cubes if you like. 7. Pour some honey or maple syrup over the top of the smoothie for sweetness. I hope you enjoy this fat burning smoothie recipe. How to do a proper split: Wajib Pemanasan! 🏃‍♀️ Jangan pernah split pas otot dingin. Lakukan kardio ringan + stretching dinamis 5–10 menit untuk area pinggul & kaki. Latih Otot Target 🧘‍♀️ Sempurnakan gerakan Low Lunge (untuk peregangan pinggul) dan Half Split (untuk paha belakang) sebelum masuk ke full split. Pinggul Harus Kotak (Squared Hips) 📐 Pastikan kedua tulang pinggul menghadap lurus ke depan, bukan miring ke samping. Ini kunci biar posisinya benar & aman. Pake Alat Bantu (Props) 🧱 Gunakan yoga blocks di kanan-kiri tangan untuk menopang berat badan kalau bokong belum menyentuh lantai. Jangan dipaksa! Atur Napas & Rileks 🌬️ Buang napas setiap kali menurunkan badan deeper. Listen to your body, kalau ada sakit yang tajam, langsung berhenti.

Hey yall! I just whipped up something warming and mega nutrient-packed to kickstart the day: Medicinal Chaga Seaweed Soup. I’ve been leaning into adding medicinal herbs and mushrooms into my cooking lately, and this one checkmarks a bunch of boxes. It’s got seaweed and Chaga mushroom, which make it super rich in minerals, antioxidants, and gut-friendly compounds. Seaweed brings iodine, calcium, magnesium, and trace minerals, plus a natural saltiness that makes things cozy without needing too much salt. Chaga is loved in the herbal world for its antioxidants and potential anti-inflammatory notes, plus it pairs perfectly with savory soups. I’m all about starting my morning with something warming and easily digestible, so this hits that sweet spot. For the flavor and texture party: - 4-5 garlic cloves (yes, garlic, because flavor and immune-boosting vibes) - 2 carrots for sweetness and color - A good bunch of seaweed (soaked, rinsed, chopped) - 2-3 tablespoons vegetable bouillon for a cozy base - A splash of soy sauce for umami depth - Tofu for protein and that silky bite - Pickled radish for a tangy crunch and a probiotic nod In total, I can pull this together in 20 minutes or less, which is perfect for busy mornings or a quick lunch that still feels nourishing. If you wanna dial the medicinal vibe up, a pinch of ginger or a dash of miso can slide in nicely.    #medicinalcooking #seaweedsoup #chagamushroom #plantbased #healthylifestyle

When I barely escaped a wildfire and lost everything…  the most common thing I heard was “at least you can build again” and “it was just a house. You’re alive.” What most people didn’t understand? That was my dream house. And yes, I was alive. But I was also shattered. And being alive doesn’t mean you don’t get to grieve what you lost. That’s what we do with pain, isn’t it? We rush to reframe it. We minimize it. We compare it away before anyone… including ourselves… has a chance to actually feel it. Two people can go through the exact same experience and one walks away fine… and one can’t stop replaying it at 2am, flinching at a tone of voice, or shutting down the second someone gets too close. That’s not weakness. That’s not being dramatic. That’s just how nervous systems work. So if you’ve ever caught yourself thinking “I shouldn’t even be this affected, other people have been through so much worse”… That thought? That’s part of the wound too. You don’t need a story that makes people gasp to deserve healing.  You don’t need to explain or justify why you feel the way you feel. If your body is stuck… it’s stuck. Full stop. And you deserve to come back to yourself… not when things get bad enough, not when you’ve finally “earned” it… right now, exactly as you are. Comment GUIDE below and I’ll send you my free guide on what I do and how to come back to yourself… so you can start feeling at home in your own body again.

Early 2024 me… This is a solid low lunge, but here’s what I’d cue differently now. In poses like Anjaneyasana, you’ll often hear “tuck your pelvis.” And for some bodies, that cue gets overused. Instead, think: lengthen your tailbone and find neutral. You want support in your low back—not compression. Also, not every body will look neutral in the same way. If you’ve got more natural curve (or let’s be honest… a little more glute), it can look like anterior tilt even when you’re well supported. That doesn’t mean you need to force yourself into a different shape. One more thing I noticed here—my front toes are lifting. That can help you find the ball of the big toe, but don’t stay there. Ground the toes back down and keep that connection. Small refinements. Big difference.

Conoces todos los beneficios que tiene Sirsasana?🤔   Sirsasana es una de las principales posturas invertidas y tiene multiples beneficios. ⭐️ Mejora el equilibrio y la concentración. ⭐️ Calma el sistema nervioso, y sirve para aliviar el estrés y la ansiedad. ⭐️ Fortalece abdominales, brazos y piernas. ⭐️ Alivia la presión de la zona lumbar y sacra. ⭐️ Mejora el sistema circulatorio. ⭐️ Reduce la retención de líquido en las piernas. ⭐️ Fortalece los pulmones, mejorando la capacidad del sistema respiratorio.   Si bien el paro de cabeza es una postura avanzada, con constancia y la practica adecuada es completamente posible de lograr! 🙌🏻   🚨 Por eso cree 10 clases especialmente enfocadas para ganar fuerza y equilibrio y poder finalmente lograr sirsasana 🤍🧘🏼‍♀️     🔗 En mi pagina toda la info del curso! Tu sistema nervioso también se entrena. Y muchos de tus hábitos diarios están decidiendo si vives en calma… o en alerta constante.” Nos acostumbramos tanto a vivir aceleradas, revisando el celular apenas abrimos los ojos, comiendo distraídas, trabajando sin pausas y durmiéndonos con la mente saturada… que creemos que eso es normal. Pero no lo es. Tu cuerpo no fue diseñado para estar hiperestimulado todo el día. Y aunque hoy el teléfono y las redes son parte de nuestra vida, también necesitamos aprender a crear pequeños momentos de regulación y presencia. Porque regular tu sistema nervioso no siempre empieza con “irse a Bali” o desaparecer del mundo. A veces empieza con cosas mucho más simples: • cómo empiezas tu mañana • cómo respiras durante el día • cómo comes • cómo descansas • cómo hablas contigo • cuánto tiempo pasas realmente presente El mindfulness no es solo “meditar”. Es aprender a volver a ti. A salir del piloto automático. A vivir con más conciencia, energía y calma. Y honestamente… cambia muchísimo la forma en que te sientes día a día 🤍 Estoy preparando algo muy especial sobre mindfulness, regulación emocional y cómo empezar a vivir con menos ruido mental y más presencia ✨ Un taller súper aterrizado para personas que sienten que su mente nunca se apaga. Si quieres ser de las primeras personas en recibir la información, comenta:MINDFULNESS 🤍 #OrnellaYoga #Mindfulness #Meditación #SistemaNervioso #BienestarEmocional
#recetassaludables #dulcessaludables
#recuerdos

Y también creo que parte de madurar es entender que no siempre vamos a reaccionar desde nuestra mejor versión. A veces acumulamos emociones, nos guardamos cosas, intentamos “estar bien” demasiado tiempo… hasta que explotamos. Y no porque seamos malas personas, sino porque muchas veces no sabemos expresar lo que sentimos a tiempo. Por eso creo que una relación sana no es la que nunca tiene conversaciones incómodas, límites o momentos difíciles. Es la que te permite hablarlos. La que te hace sentir que puedes expresarte sin miedo. La que, incluso en el conflicto, tiene intención de escuchar, cuidar y comprender ✨ Porque al final creo que gestionar emociones también es aprender a comunicarnos antes de llegar al límite 🤍 ¿Ustedes sienten que les cuesta expresar lo que sienten a tiempo? 👀

Been making these mini cheesecakes for over 10 years now, and they never fail  Ingredients:  For filling:  - 1 lb cream cheese  - 1/4 c heavy cream  - 3/4 c sugar  - 2 eggs - 1 tsp vanilla extract  For crust:  - 1 1/2 c crushed graham crackers  - 1/2 c melted butter  Instructions:  1. Preheat oven to 325F.  2. Prepare graham cracker crust by coming graham crackers and melted butter. Mix to combine.  3. Pour crumbs into baking pan of choice, and press firmly. (I used a mini cheesecake pan) 4. In a bowl, using a hand mixer or stand mixer, beat cream cheese until creamy.  5. Add sugar and mix again.  6. Add heavy cream and vanilla extract, and stir until combined. Scrape the sides of your bowl, then mix again.  7. With mixer on low speed, add eggs one at a time. Scrape the sides of your bowl one more time, then mix again.  8. Pour cheesecake batter into prepared pans, and place pans on cookie sheet before placing in the oven.  9. Bake on the center rack of your oven for 20 minutes (for mini cheesecakes), and 50-60 minutes for whole cheesecake. Once finished baking, crack the oven door and allow it to gradually cool before removing from the oven. After removing them from the oven, allow it to cool to room temperature before storing in the fridge. Enjoy!❤️🩷❤️ #bakingrecipe #cheesecake #valentinesday

Bạn đang tập Yoga vì sức khỏe hay vì sự công nhận từ người khác? 🤔 Chắc hẳn bạn đã từng nghe câu: "Tập Yoga để khỏe, để sống vui vẻ hơn." Nhưng có bao giờ bạn tự hỏi: Liệu mình có đang tập Yoga chỉ vì... để khoe với người khác không? 👉 Yoga vì sức khỏe: Khi bạn thật sự muốn chăm sóc cơ thể và tâm trí, không cần phải tìm kiếm sự công nhận từ ai cả. Mỗi lần tập là bạn đang làm điều tốt cho chính mình, không phải vì ai đó nhìn vào. 👉 Yoga vì sự công nhận: Nếu bạn chỉ tập Yoga để có thể "pose" đẹp trên Instagram hay làm người khác phải trầm trồ về khả năng giữ thăng bằng của mình, thì bạn có thể đang bỏ qua cái cốt lõi của Yoga: sự kết nối với chính mình. Hãy nhớ, Yoga không phải là cuộc thi. Đừng để những cái nhìn ngoài kia khiến bạn mất đi sự tự tin và cảm giác an yên khi tập luyện. Điều quan trọng không phải là bạn làm được bao nhiêu tư thế khó mà là bạn cảm nhận thế nào trong từng chuyển động, từng hơi thở. 🌿💖 Hãy để Yoga giúp bạn làm chủ cơ thể và tâm trí, không phải để làm hài lòng người khác. #yogalife #wellness #passion #sunshineyogastudio

Little morning thoughts this morning as I was chatting with a few friends that have chronic health issues, and they were asking me questions about how do I deal with military life and always having to start over?!  I honestly think it’s really fun. My personality is one where its hard to do the same things all the time & in the same environments. If you have studied human design, that’s actually what mine says.  YET don’t get me wrong, it’s never easy and it does affect my flareups. My routines help to keep my nervous system balanced , especially this time around. Thats the key in life honestly > remain in a neutral mood, once you start to spiral 🌀 ( which I jokingly call the Sarah Spiral ) it doesn’t support you.  Things that really help support me everyday >>>  ✔️ Morning Journaling. Get all your thoughts out! Let it flow & take time to feel your emotions before jumping into tasks.  ✔️ A Slow morning and night time routine is key for me & many of my clients- you must create personalized routines for you that you can be consistent with & look forward too!  ✔️ Movement- movement allows you to release energy & emotions!!! If you are not moving you are storing these up- RELEASE. If you find a positive outlet for your emotions you will solve about 90% of your problems.  ✔️Breath-work & Nature - This is KEY. Ever realize how much you hold your breath?! Whens the last time you ever sat in nature & really focused on your breath- maybe never! Both Nature & breathing help purify your body and ground you energetically- that isn’t woo crap its real. Exactly why the city can put you into fight or flight.

The devil is in the details. 👀 Most people who practice yoga are doing one thing at a time..moving the body, or following the breath, or half-listening to the teacher while mentally composing a grocery list. True alignment is when all three come together simultaneously. Body placed with intention. Breath moving freely through it. Attention fully present inside the experience rather than observing it from a distance. When that happens…and it takes practice, real practice…the pose stops being a shape you are making and becomes something you are actually living inside. And that quality of being completely present in your own body is what the entire tradition has always been pointing toward. This is why two people can do the exact same posture and have completely different experiences. One is performing it. The other is practicing it. You cannot see the difference from the outside. You can only feel it from the inside. Yoga doesn’t happen to you. It becomes possible the moment you bring your whole self (body, breath, and attention) into the same room at the same time. Once you feel that, you cannot unfeel it. Comment YOGA SCHEDULE and I’ll send you our class schedule at Jai, where this is what we show up for every single session. 🎯 #coquitlamyoga #yoga #yvryoga #vancouver #vancouveryoga

This is what actually happens when you practice yoga twice a week. And I don’t mean the flexibility. That’s just the part that happens to your body while everything else quietly changes underneath it. The reality most people don’t expect: 🔍 You sleep differently. Not longer but deeper. Because your nervous system finally gets the signal that it is allowed to let go. Most people don’t realise how much they’ve been holding until it starts to release. 🔍 You find the gap. That tiny space between something happening and you reacting to it. Yoga doesn’t remove the difficult moments. It gives you a fraction of a second to choose how you meet them. That fraction of a second changes everything. 🔍 The people around you notice before you do. Six to eight weeks in, something shifts that is visible from the outside before you can name it on the inside. More present. Less reactive. More you. Yoga doesn’t make your life easier. It makes you more capable of meeting your life. Two sessions a week is not a fitness commitment. It’s the decision to stop reacting to your life and start responding to it. I saw someone say yoga is just stretching and honestly…same. That is exactly what we have made it look like. We took one of the most sophisticated systems of inner engineering ever created and turned it into a flexibility class. Outstanding work, everyone. Here is what most people don't know. Yoga means union. Not stretch. Not movement. The dissolution of the boundary between what you experience as yourself and everything else that exists. Patanjali gave us eight limbs of practice. Eight. The physical postures are one of them. The other seven are concerned with something far more fundamental: how you relate to others, how you breathe, how you direct your attention, and ultimately the nature of the one who is doing all of this. We kept the one limb that photographs well. The other seven have been quietly waiting. At Jai, we teach the whole system. Not just the poses, but the philosophy, the breathwork, the inquiry that makes the movement actually mean something. Because a practice that only lives in your body will only ever take you so far. The instruction manual exists. Most studios just forgot to hand it out. I used to be so self-conscious about myself. I cared too much about what people thought, how I looked, whether I was good enough. It became exhausting constantly trying to fit into everyone else’s expectations while slowly losing myself in the process. Then one day I asked myself, “What’s the point of living if I’m not even proud of who I am?” That question stayed in my mind for a long time. So I started choosing myself little by little. I went to India alone for my 300-hour yoga teacher training, not realizing how much it would change me from the inside out. Being there taught me that healing doesn’t happen when you become perfect. It happens when you finally stop being at war with yourself. Somewhere between the early mornings, long practices, quiet moments, and meeting people from around the world, I slowly found confidence in simply being me. Not perfect. Not fearless. Just real. And honestly, that version of me feels so much more beautiful than the girl who spent her whole life trying to be accepted by everyone else. 🤍 #yoga#yogainspiration #yogateachertraining
Kids yoga showed me that healing doesn’t always happen in silence. Sometimes it happens in laughter, messy poses, and little voices saying, ‘I did it! #kidsyoga#yoga #meditation #pranayama
Every tiny stretch, every giggle during yoga class, every child choosing peace over frustration those moments quietly changed my life. #kidsyoga #autismawareness #yoga #meditation #pranayama

If you were active before and during pregnancy, the urge to move again after birth makes complete sense. But here’s what most women don’t realise , your postpartum body isn’t just tired. It’s different. This isn’t the kind of rest you needed pre-pregnancy. What your body went through during birth is on another level entirely. It needs a different kind of restoration. I’ve seen mamas jump straight into intense core work during confinement, thinking it’ll speed things up. But it can actually weaken the core and pelvic floor further and slow recovery down, or make things worse. If you want to move, start with a short walk. Light stretching. Breathe into your body, not against it. Postpartum is also an invitation to practise surrender. To accept where you are right now. To slow down and honour the changes in your body, knowing your life has shifted too. And it’s one of the most powerful times to practise gratitude. A little miracle happened through you. You don’t have to earn your recovery. You just have to respect it. You’ve got this, mama.  如果你在孕前和孕期一直保持活跃，产后想重新动起来是完全可以理解的。 但大多数女性没有意识到的是——你的产后身体不仅仅是疲惫，它已经变得不同了。 这不是你孕前需要的那种休息。你的身体在分娩中所经历的一切，完全是另一个层次。它需要一种不同的恢复方式。 我见过很多妈妈在坐月子期间直接进行高强度的核心训练，以为能加快恢复。但这实际上可能进一步削弱核心肌群和骨盆底肌，反而拖慢恢复进程，甚至让情况更糟。 如果你想活动，先从短距离散步开始。做一些轻柔的拉伸。吸气时顺应身体，而非与之对抗。 产后也是一次邀请——去练习臣服，接纳当下的自己，慢下来，尊重身体的变化，明白你的生活也已经发生了改变。 同时，这也是练习感恩的最有力量的时刻之一。一个微小的奇迹通过你发生了。 你不必去“挣得”你的恢复。你只需要尊重它。 你可以的，妈妈。 #postpartumrecovery #pelvicfloor #postpartumbody #childbirth #newmom

To the brilliant, capable, and deeply tired woman…. You’ve been working so hard. You know it. But your nervous system can’t tell the difference between doing it all for your career, your family, your team, or your dreams. It just knows it’s been running. For too long. Maybe no one told you that regulation is performance. Your nervous system doesn’t negotiate with your ambition. It just burns out quietly, until it can’t. The reset isn’t weakness. Legs up the wall is one of the simplest nervous system resets you can do. When you lie here and breathe slowly, your vagus nerve senses that you’re calm and sends that signal to the brain — shifting you out of fight-or-flight and into rest and digest. Research published in the Journal of Physical Therapy Science found that leg elevation significantly improves circulation and reduces lower limb swelling  — especially for those who sit or stand for long hours. 5 minutes. That’s all it takes. Save this for when you need it. 倒箭式（腿靠墙上举）是最简单的神经系统重启方式之一。当你躺下并缓慢呼吸时，你的迷走神经会感知到你的平静状态，并将这一信号传递给大脑——帮助你从“战斗或逃跑”模式切换到“休息与消化”模式。发表于《物理治疗科学杂志》的一项研究发现，抬高双腿能显著改善血液循环，减轻下肢水肿——尤其对需要久坐或久站的人群非常有益。只需5分钟。保存下来，等你需要时再用。 #legsupthewall #yogaathome #nervoussystemregulation #resetroutine #reset

Here’s what most moms don’t get told after birth: Your body just did the most physically demanding thing it will ever do. And unlike a sprained ankle or a torn muscle — the recovery doesn’t follow the same rules as before. Your body before pregnancy? It knew how to heal itself. You rested, you recovered, you moved on. After pregnancy it’s different. Your pelvic floor has been through so much — carrying the weight of your baby for 9 months, and then the birth itself. It doesn’t just go back to normal on its own. Your core muscles — the deep ones — they separated during pregnancy to make room for your baby. And unless you actually work on reconnecting them, they stay that way. That’s why you still feel the tummy pooch. The back pain. The leaking when you sneeze or laugh. The feeling that something just isn’t right. That’s not you being weak. That’s your body waiting for the right kind of help. Not just rest. Not just “ease back into exercise.” Not just hoping it sorts itself out. Real recovery. The right way. At the right pace. This is what Radiant Return is about. DM me RESTORE and let’s get your recovery started properly.  以下是大多数妈妈在产后不会被告知的事情： 你的身体刚刚完成了它这一生中最耗费体力的任务。而且，不同于脚踝扭伤或肌肉撕裂——这一次的恢复，规则完全不同。 怀孕前的你？你的身体知道如何自我修复。休息一下，恢复过来，然后继续前行。 但怀孕之后就不一样了。 你的盆底肌承受了太多——整整9个月承载着宝宝的重量，再加上分娩本身的过程。它不会自己就恢复正常。 你的核心肌肉——那些深层的肌肉——在孕期为了给宝宝腾出空间而发生了分离。除非你主动去重建它们的连接，否则它们会一直保持分离状态。这就是为什么你依然觉得小肚子收不回去。还会腰酸背痛。打喷嚏或大笑时会漏尿。总觉得哪里不太对劲。 那不是因为你不够坚强。 而是你的身体在等待正确的帮助。 不仅仅是休息。 不仅仅是“慢慢开始运动”。 不仅仅是祈祷它会自己好起来。 真正的恢复。用正确的方式。以合适的节奏。 这就是Radiant Return的意义所在。 私信我“RESTORE”，让我帮你正确开启产后恢复之路。 #postnatalrecovery #postpartumbody #diastasisrecti #postpartumjourney #newmomtips

Most people don’t realise they’re running on empty until the weekend hits and they still can’t switch off. Energy isn’t just about how much sleep you got or how many coffees you needed. It’s about whether the way you’re living is returning something to you — or only taking. If you ticked sustaining: notice what’s contributing to that. Is it your environment, your boundaries, your movement, your people? Name it — because what you can name, you can protect. If you ticked depleting: this isn’t a character flaw. It’s data. It’s your nervous system telling you something in your week isn’t aligned with how you’re actually built to function. The question isn’t “how do I push through?” The question is: what needs to change? Energy management isn’t a productivity hack. It’s how you stay well enough to keep showing up for the things and people that matter. #energy #womenwellness #nervoussystemregulation #vitalityintensive #takecareofyourself

Working out and lifting as a seasoned woman is less about chasing youth and more about protecting the life you want to keep living.  A strong core becomes your anchor, it supports your spine, stabilizes your balance, protects your joints, and keeps everyday movements graceful instead of painful. Even when it isn’t easy, every rep is an investment in mobility, independence, and vitality.  Strength training is how a mature woman stays powerful in her body and peaceful in her mind, a true Yogini aging plan. 🧘‍♀️🤩 💜✨☮️ #aging #women #strength #lifting #gymtok

ท่านี้เป็นท่าโยคะฟลายที่ต้องใช้ทั้ง “แรง–บาลานซ์–ความยืดหยุ่น” พร้อมกัน ร่างกายกำลังอยู่ในลักษณะเอียงกลางอากาศ โดยใช้ผ้าเป็นจุดพยุงหลักที่สะโพก/ลำตัว แล้วเปิดขาเป็นเส้นทแยง—ขาหนึ่งเหยียดขึ้นสูง อีกขาหนึ่งยืดออกด้านหลัง พร้อมเอื้อมมือแตะเบาๆ เพื่อช่วยคุมสมดุล ท่านี้ต้องอาศัยแกนกลางลำตัว (core) ที่แข็งแรงมาก และการควบคุมร่างกายที่ละเอียดสุด ๆ เพราะน้ำหนักไม่ได้อยู่บนพื้นเต็มที่ ความท้าทายของท่านี้คือ * ต้อง “เชื่อใจร่างกาย” และผ้าไปพร้อมกัน * การทรงตัวอยู่ในมุมเอียงแบบนี้ ถ้าคุมแกนไม่ดีจะเสียบาลานซ์ทันที * ต้องเปิดสะโพกและยืด hamstring ได้ดี เพื่อให้เส้นขาดูยาวและไม่หักงอ ส่วนความสวยงามคือมันมีความ “ไหลลื่นและเบา” มาก เหมือนร่างกายลอยอยู่กลางอากาศ เส้นขาที่ยืดออกทำให้เกิดไลน์ที่ยาวและสง่า ดูทั้งแข็งแรงและอ่อนช้อยในเวลาเดียวกัน โดยเฉพาะมุมศีรษะและแขนที่ผ่อนคลาย ทำให้ภาพรวมไม่แข็ง แต่ดูพลิ้วและมีศิลปะมาก พูดง่าย ๆ คือ เป็นท่าที่ผสมความ “แกร่ง” กับ “นุ่ม” ได้ลงตัวมาก เห็นแล้วรู้เลยว่าควบคุมร่างกายได้ระดับสูงเลย😁❤️ Yoga Station By Natcha#yogastationbynatcha #ดันขึ้นหน้าฟีดที #โยคะประชาชื่น #โยคะฟลาย #ฮิตในtiktok

ท่ายืนก้มตัว (Standing Forward Fold) ในโยคะ เรียกเป็นภาษาสันสกฤตว่า “อุตตานาสนะ (Uttanasana)” ลักษณะเด่นของท่านี้: * ยืนตรงแล้วพับตัวลงจากสะโพก * ศีรษะโน้มลงใกล้ขา หรือสอดเข้าไปด้านหลังขา (แบบในภาพเป็นเวอร์ชันยืดลึก) * มือวางบนพื้นหรือจับข้อเท้า ประโยชน์: * ยืดกล้ามเนื้อหลังและต้นขาด้านหลัง (Hamstrings) * ช่วยผ่อนคลายความเครียด * กระตุ้นการไหลเวียนเลือดไปสมอง#yogastationbynatcha #ดันขึ้นหน้าฟีดที #yogamat #โยคะประชาชื่น #ฮิตในtiktok

I found a park near my house with monkey bars and pull-up bars, so I went there with my youngest, who is flying the coop in a couple of days, and decided to try the monkey bars. I had tried them at the gym months ago and couldn’t get past the first rung. I was never good at this kind of thing as a kid, either. I did them for the first time in my life at 62. My son cheered me on and gave me a couple of pointers that actually helped. I was the mom being coached, trying to swing from one bar to the next without overthinking it. In my latest reel, I asked: if I can learn pull-ups in my 60s, what else can I do? This was one answer. Monkey bars. At 62, I’ll take that. And to top it off it was fun!  I plan on returning to the outdoor fitness area to play around more.  What would you like to try that, until now, you thought it was too late for? #thisis62 #activeaging #calisthenics

One of the things I’ve learned in improv is to ask myself: if this is true, what else is true? For instance, if in an improvised imaginary world the sky is purple, then what else is true in that world? What else follows from that? I’ve been thinking about that with pull-ups. If it’s true that I learned to do overhand pull-ups in my early 60s, after starting with a partially torn rotator cuff, with long arms, as a woman over 60, then what else is true of me? What else can I do? What else have I assumed I couldn’t do because of my age, my body, my circumstances, or some story I had been telling myself for years? This doesn’t have to be about pull-ups or fitness goals. It can apply to any part of life. For me, the question goes much further back. If it’s true that I pulled myself out of being a single mom on welfare in my mid-forties, then what else was I capable of? If I managed to rebuild my life then, what else could I figure out later? If something I once thought was out of reach became part of my actual life, what else have I not even tried yet? Today, after I did these pull-ups, that question came back to me: if this is true, what else is true? What’s something you’ve done that made you wonder what else might be possible? #ActiveAging #WomenOver60 #PullUpsAfter60

Last March, my husband, Phil, took me to Salón Tenampa in Plaza Garibaldi in Mexico City. He used to go there with friends and colleagues when he was a photojournalist living in CDMX in his early thirties. He told me it has changed a lot since then, but it still felt special. Plaza Garibaldi is known for its mariachis, and @salontenampa has been there since the 1920s. We didn’t have reservations, but because it was just the two of us, we got in pretty fast and got a booth. The food was wonderful, the service was next level, and it felt nostalgic.  Then Phil asked the mariachis for “Por un amor,” which I did not expect. He sings that song sometimes, and it always irks me because the chorus is “pobre de mí” (poor me).  But hearing it sung by mariachis, with all that feeling, was something else. It was even romantic coming from Phil.  If you go, bring cash to request songs from the mariachis, although many may take electronic payment too. They really do give it their all. Have you ever gone somewhere with your partner that felt like stepping into their past? #mariachis #CDMX #plazagaribaldi  El pasado marzo, Phil me llevó al Salón Tenampa, en la plaza Garibaldi, en Ciudad de México. Él solía ir allí con amigos y compañeros cuando vivía en CDMX, a sus treinta y pico, y trabajaba como fotoperiodista. Me dijo que había cambiado mucho desde entonces, pero aun así nos pareció un sitio especial. La plaza Garibaldi es conocida por sus mariachis, y el Salón Tenampa lleva allí desde los años veinte. No teníamos reserva, pero como éramos solo los dos, entramos bastante rápido y nos dieron una mesa en un reservado. La comida estaba buenísima, el servicio fue de primera, y el ambiente estupendo. Entonces Phil les pidió a los mariachis “Por un amor”, cosa que no me esperaba. A veces él canta esa canción y siempre me da un poco de rabia por el coro (Pobre de mí). Pero escucharla cantada por mariachis, con todo ese sentimiento, fue otra cosa. Incluso romántico. Si vais, llevad efectivo para pedir canciones a los mariachis, aunque seguramente muchos acepten algún tipo de pago electrónico. Se dejan el alma. ¿Alguna vez habéis ido con vuestra pareja a un lugar que parecía llevaros directamente a su pasado?

A few months ago, I was scared every time I jumped up to these bars. I still did it, but I was never sure I’d make it. I was still doing pull-ups by yanking with my whole body. Then I finally made the brain-lat connection, which I talked about in a previous post, and everything changed. My pull-ups started feeling more efficient because I was finally using the muscles I was supposed to be using. And before anyone corrects me: this is a neutral grip pull-up, not a chin-up. Chin-ups are underhand, not a parallel grip. And yes, I also do overhand pull-ups (see previous reels). The internet correctors are everywhere, for real.  I started working toward my first pull-up after 60 while recovering from a partially torn rotator cuff, after more than two years of dialing back upper body work. I had long arms, little upper body strength, and a body that was definitely not recovering as it used to at younger ages. So the fact that I’m almost 63 and can jump to the bars, do the pull-ups, and walk away without feeling wrecked still feels a little magical to me. It was not a straight road. I had setbacks, including injuries to both elbows, and I had to stop certain workouts for a while. But I worked around it. I recovered while I kept training in whatever way I could. If I’ve learned anything, it’s that feeling strong in my 60s helps a lot with the setbacks and weirdness that come with aging. Not because strength prevents everything, but because it grounds me. It’s interesting how learning to do pull-ups after 60 has become about so much more than pull-ups. It’s been about patience, stubbornness, setbacks, recovery, and realizing my body is still willing to learn. What’s one thing you’ve done scared, but did anyway? #pullupsafter60 #pullupdrills #thisis62

I told myself if I didn’t have kids by 25, I wouldn’t be a mom. Well, life had other plans, and I had my first baby three months shy of my 38th birthday.  At nearly four months along, I experienced a threatened miscarriage and was placed on bedrest for two weeks. It was terrifying. I sobbed in the ER, thinking I was losing my baby. But Chloe held on like the trouper she is. She was born in Sevilla, Spain on a Friday during Feria. That year, Mother’s Day in Spain fell the next Sunday, so she was quite literally my Mother’s Day gift.  From day one, Chloe had this look that said, “I know more than you think I do.” She still does. She’s been traveling solo since the age of 9 (having family in other countries helped), and I knew that letting her go was how I’d help her grow. At 18, she moved to California with my sister @lauralcb, her godmother. I cried my eyes out, but I never once told her not to go. A few months later, she flew solo to Australia. Since then, she’s seen more of the world than most people twice her age. We meet wherever we can: Lake Tahoe, Madrid, Sarasota or some place in between. The reel is from my latest trip, where I went to Kirkwood, her place of work, and enjoyed seeing her in her element. Today, Chloe turns 25. She’s a trained EMT and a ski patroller. A year ago, she narrowly escaped death in a hiking accident, but in true Chloe form, she came back stronger. I swear she has nine lives. Brave, noble, kind-hearted, and filled with grit, she is everything I admire in a human being.  She’s now dealing with doctors and procedures to get some health-related answers, as we share a recent diagnosis of SVT (supraventricular tachycardia) although mine doesn’t interfere with my life, and hers does. But she still lives to the max.  Happy, happy birthday to @cxn_33, the woman who made me a mother. May the 4th be with you, always. I love you more than words will ever convey, and I’ll be forever grateful that you exist. Please help me wish Chloe a happy 25th! What words of wisdom would you share with her? #thisis25 #skipatroller #mothersday

Yesterday I had one of those aha moments that’s hard to explain unless you’ve been chasing a skill for a long time. For the first time, at 62, I felt my lats fire up and do most of the work in a pull-up, the way they’re supposed to. I started training for pull-ups at 60, basically just hanging from the bar. I was coming out of a partially torn rotator cuff. Over the past two years, I’ve had to dial things back more than once to avoid messing up my shoulder again. Then I had to work around and recover from lifter’s elbow, which came from too much overhead lifting in BodyPump class. So progress has not been a straight line. I could do pull-ups before yesterday, but I’d bring my knees up into my chest and help myself that way. Yesterday I got 3.5 without doing that. For the first time, I truly understood and felt what it means to pull with my back. The strength was already there. I just didn’t know how to access it. I knew it in theory, but I hadn’t felt it. Like standing in front of a door with the key in my hand, but not knowing how to unlock it. And then, suddenly, I did. My next goal is 5 pull-ups. For the first time, that feels less like wishful thinking and more like something I can actually get to. It made me think about how often this happens in life, too. We keep working at something, adjusting, getting frustrated, backing off, trying again… and then one day something clicks. Have you ever had that happen? With exercise, work, creativity, relationships, anything? #pullups #pullupsafter60 #thisis62

If you’re in Mexico City, make time for the Museo Nacional de Antropología. It’s inside Bosque de Chapultepec and it’s big. We thought we’d be in and out… we spent about 4 hours and could have stayed longer. You’ll see everything from the Aztec Sun Stone to entire rooms dedicated to different regions and cultures. It’s one of those museums where you actually slow down and read. We also had brunch there and the food was spectacular. Not something I expected at a museum. I also bought a beautiful handmade shawl at the gift store.  A few practical things: • Hours: Tuesday to Sunday, 9 am to 6 pm (closed Mondays) • Entrance: about 95 pesos (around $5 USD) • Go early. When we left, the line was long. Have you been? #MexicoCity #activetravel #cdmx

Improv sometimes gives me a reason to dress up and be whoever I want to be. I was a painfully shy kid. I was scared of drama class and hated that I had to be in it.  And yet… I still ended up in the spotlight in other ways. Public speaking, interpreting languages, writing and publishing books… But I didn’t try improv until 59. Musical improv at 62. And it’s a whole lot of fun. We laugh a lot. I get out of my head for a while. It’s a break from everything. I’ve met such interesting people through it, and I even get to do it with my husband, which I never would have imagined years ago. I’ve gotten bolder with age. Although I was pretty darn bold before, taking on projects and activities that were way over my head or that I was scared stiff of.  And yes, getting older can feel super freeing. But it’s not the only way to feel free. I do wish I had leaned harder into my quirks earlier. I wish I had cared less about what people thought. If you’re holding back, don’t wait until you’re older to try something that feels fun, even if it also feels a little scary. What’s something you’ve been wanting to try but haven’t? Use controlled eccentric phases for happy tendons!  Tendons love tempo bc they adapt more slowly than muscles do. Slowing a movement down increases time under tension, which gives the tendon a longer, steadier load to respond to and strengthen from.  Too fast or sloppy reps can overload irritated tendons. 😵 Slowing it down creates smoother force distribution, as well as improves your awareness of your body’s positioning and how to stabilize your joints properly thru movement and under load. TLDR: Don’t rush thru the lowering phase of the life (when gravity is working in your favor), but keep control and awareness of the muscle engagement while it’s lengthening as you lower and shortening as you lift. If there’s one thing I’ve learned from the best handbalancers on the internet, it’s this: 👉 Time under tension (TUT) is everything. That’s why I usually practice near a wall — it helps fine-tune my alignment and lets me focus on building control and endurance. My goal is about one minute of quality TUT per set. Here are a few tips that help me stay consistent: 💡 Plan your exit. Always know how you’ll come down safely. 💡 Do multiple sets. Aim for 5–10, depending on your level. 💡 Use a timer. I like to start with 10 seconds to warm up, then add 10 seconds each round — 10, 20, 30, and so on. 💡 Use the wall. It’s a great teacher — you’ll get instant feedback on your alignment and balance. I used to call Dolphin Pose “a pose with a porpoise” — until I learned dolphins and porpoises aren’t the same. So now, it’s officially Porpoise Pose! And the porpoise here is this: In poses like headstand and other inversions, we want to engage the muscles under the shoulders — think serratus anterior and lower traps — instead of relying on the upper shoulders and neck. Even if you’ve mastered headstand, spending time in Porpoise Pose builds strength, awareness, and a strong foundation for safer, more sustainable inversions. Having teenage children means that I stay updated on the latest TikTok trends. From Stanley mugs to odd food recipes, if it’s trending, we are interested. When my 14-year-old daughter told me Pilates has become quite popular with the TikTok generation, I was eager to reveal that her “old man” was a longtime practitioner. She was stunned, and probably way less interested in Pilates… but still. I began Pilates with my old yoga teacher, Don Scheumann, who had been a student of Romana Kryzanowska (Joseph Pilates Senior Student) in NYC back in the 1980s. Although Don’s classes were called “yoga” on the schedule, in truth, we were mostly doing Pilates Mat Work with meditation and yoga blended in. Years later, I went on to formally train in Pilates Mat with Tom McCook at the Center of Balance in Mountain View, California. Although I never intended to teach Pilates, I wanted to learn more about the method so that I could improve my yoga classes. I find the Pilates method to be wonderfully precise, and Pilates teachers to have a sophisticated understanding of movement and anatomy. Of course, there are many overlaps with the Pilates method and yoga since Pilates himself had studied yoga and the other Physical Culture methods of the time. From time to time, I do teach classical Pilates Mat in dedicated classes, but for the most part, I try to instill the Contrology principles in my yoga class. If you pay close attention, you will discover many overlaps between yoga and Pilates. For example, in this clip, I am demonstrating a hybrid of Pilates Jack Knife with the Shoulderstand of yoga. So, if you have taken yoga classes from me over the last 20 years, you’ve been exposed to the Pilates method (whether you knew it or not). Have you tried Pilates? If your hands had six-pack abs, you'd probably spend a lot more time strengthening them. Wrist Ups are a great "ab exercise" for your hands that can be scaled to fit the individual. Perform the Wrist Up by squeezing the fingertips into the floor, which in turn "pops" the wrist up. As a beginner, start your Wrist Up practice while on hands and knees. As you get stronger, try the Wrist Up in other positions such as plank. For better control, it’s okay to do one hand at a time. Avoid hyperextending the fingers here. If your fingers bend backwards, that ain't right. Instead, think of "microbending" the finger knuckles to maintain your structure. For bonus body awareness, notice how the Wrist Up is an intrinsic part of movements that you perform often, such as stepping forward in Warrior (lunge) position. Wrist Ups should help you feel stronger and more stable when spending time on your hands. Lotus pose is more than just sitting in lotus; it symbolizes the archetype of external hip rotation. As teachers, it's crucial that we comprehend how to modify this movement archetype based on the student's condition each day. This means the teacher should offer options to make the pose both "easier" and more attainable, as well as options to make it "harder" and more aspirational. To achieve this goal, I present to you 7 stages of Lotus progression. Can YOU SEE the fundamental movement remains consistent across all 7 variations? This advice on drop backs may be a little controversial, but here goes: Many teachers will tell you to keep the heels down when doing drop backs. Unfortunately, this isn’t going to work for everyone… As a person with so-so flexibility, I had to figure out the technique to complete many of the advanced sequences in Ashtanga, such as drop backs. If you have stiff ankles (like me), it’s going to be difficult to keep the center of gravity far enough forward to drop back with control. Some people will start with their feet really wide (wider than the mat even), or turn their feet out to get the center of gravity far enough forward. Another option is to lift your heel. When dropping back: Go as far as you can into the backbend, then “release” into the drop back by lifting the heel and landing softly on your hands. When standing up: Practice rocking the weight forward and backward in sync with your breath: Inhale forward into the legs foundation while walking your hands toward the feet, Exhale backward into the arms foundation and feel a big stretch of the chest and upper back. At a point, it will be easier to stand up than it will be to come down again. Hopefully this video will make things clear. Day 137/365 – Kula: The Power of Coming Together ✨💛 This right here—this is everything. In Sanskrit, the word kula means community, tribe, family of the heart. And today, as we gather in circle, I’m reminded why this work matters so deeply. A retreat isn’t just a getaway. It’s a coming home. To ourselves. To each other. To what’s real, what’s sacred, what’s ready to rise. In kula, we hold space for one another. We laugh, we cry, we soften, we grow. We witness and are witnessed in the most authentic way—without masks, without pressure, just pure presence. I’m so honored to be here, surrounded by incredible women who are saying YES to their journey inward. Together, we remember: we’re not meant to do this alone. Here’s to the magic of kula. To connection, transformation, and sisterhood. #Day137 #Kula #CommunityIsMedicine #YogaRetreatVibes #TogetherWeRise #Sisterhood #YogaEveryDamnDay #HeartWork #RealConnection

Day 97!  Imagine the gentle glow of the morning light through your window, sitting with a fresh cup of coffee, the warmth of a smile from a stranger, or the quiet hum of your own breath, as you settle into stillness. These moments, seemingly simple, are treasures waiting to be acknowledged.  By anchor into gratitude, we invite a vibration of abundance into our lives. Each moment of appreciation shifts are perspective, turning every day occurrences into profound blessings.  Today, I challenge you to pause, look around, and celebrate the little things that make life, extraordinary.  #Day97 #YogaEveryDay #365DaysOfYoga #GratitudeFrequency. #Abundance. #simplejoy

Day 96/365 days of yoga.  It’s not about the number of friends anymore – it’s about the quality of the souls that we surround ourselves with. Today I am grateful for those intimate conversations, for shared laughter, and of course the soulful energy of our yoga community.  On the mat and off, these moments remind me that true connection is a form of self-care – a secret space where vulnerability blossoms into strength, and love.  #Day96 #YogaEveryday #MagicalConnections #YogaCommunity #Girlfriends

Day 95/365 days of yoga.  Friends don’t miss the small moments, the conversations. Every moment is pure magic if you let it be.  Today, I was reminded of that in a conversation. We are a mirror for each other, reflecting back parts of our own light, and our own shadow. In our shared humanity, we see pieces of ourselves – our hopes, our struggles, our beauty.  “ You are not a drop in the ocean. You are the entire ocean in a drop.” Rumí  knew what he was talking about.  #Day95 #YogaEveryDay #EmbodiedWisdom #WeAreMirrors #RumiWisdom #Interconnectedness. #ReflectYourLight.

It’s these moments when the world seems to vast, to painful, and my mind struggles to comprehend the sorrow that is folding around us. Yet, even in deep grief, I turned to my practice as a sanctuary. Yoga, reminds me to sit with the pain, to honor every tear, every ache, and to keep an open heart. It teaches us that feeling it all is not a sign of weakness, but is a testament to our capacity for love and connection.  To the Bibas family, to all who are hurting, and to every soul in need of solace: you are seen, you are held, and you are not alone.  May our shared vulnerability, be a source of strength, and may our open hearts light the way through these dark times.  #day94 #OpenHeart #Grieving #healing #YogaForTheSoul #Compassion #holdingspace

Day 93/365 days of yoga.  Your core is more than just abs – it’s your entire center, your foundation, your inner fire. Strengthening it is about stability, balance, and moving through life with more ease. Today, I tapped into a little core activation and some functional movement, because you can’t just build strength from stillness. 💪🏼 #Day93 #CoreActivation #Purpose #Strong #YogaEveryDay

Oh how I love me a good conversation with my younger self? @Jennae Cecelia Poetry thank you for starting this trend. Today I was reminded of how far I’ve come and how resilient I am ✨ Day 92/365 days of yoga.  #day92 #yogaeveryday #youngerself #healing #movement

Day 91/365 days of yoga.  The truth is, nothing real is ever found in the noise. It’s in the stillness where I remember – I am already home.  Slow down.  Pause.  Take a deep breath.  #Day91 #YogaEveryDay #365DaysOfYoga #Sacredpause #SlowDown

Day 90/365 days of yoga.  Mondays always hold a special kind of magic.  How do I wanna show up? What energy am I bringing to the game?  How do I want to respond to the world around me? You see, yoga isn’t about what happens on the mat. It’s about who we are becoming – moment by moment, breath by breath. The asana, well that’s just training ground for life. The place where we practice presence, resilience, and alignment, so when life moves fast, we are ready to know how to move with it.  So here’s to day 90, stepping into it with purpose, resilience and alignment. What’s your intention this week? Drop it below.  #Day90 #NewWeek #NewEnergy #BodiedLiving #YogaEveryDay.

Most students think yoga poses are about getting into the shape. What often gets missed is what creates the pose. One of the most important principles in asana is oppositional movement. Two parts of the body move in opposite directions at the same time to create lift, length, support, and stability. For example: Press the hands down as the hips lift in downward dog. Press foot into hand and hand into foot in chapasana. Press foot into leg and leg into foot in tree pose. The pose becomes more alive when opposing actions are present. Without them, it is easy to hang out in the posture and miss the deeper experience. This is the kind of detail that changes not only how you practice, but how you teach and it’s exactly the kind of depth my 200 hour is filled with. Most people assume standing split is limited by the standing leg hamstrings. Sometimes it is. But very often the real limiter is the lifted leg! In standing split, the top leg has no floor beneath it to press into the way it does in regular splits. That means the hip flexors need enough length to allow the leg to rise, and the glutes need enough strength to actively lift it. Standing split is also a forward fold. The more you can compress your torso toward the standing thigh, the more available range you create for the lifted leg. This is why flexibility alone does not always change the pose. Mobility, strength, and active compression all matter. If you want to improve standing split, train the pose from multiple angles and not just passive stretching. We’ve been lied to about rest. We’ve been told that if we’re tired, we just need more sleep. But how many times have you slept 8 hours… and still woke up exhausted? Because sleep and rest are not the same thing. You can sleep all night and still feel depleted when your spirit, your mind, or your environment hasn’t been held. There are different ways the body calls for rest. Not just physical… but deeper. 8 pathways of rest: Physical — when your body needs to be supported, not pushed Mental — when your mind needs quiet, not more input Emotional — when you need space to be real, not “okay” Social — when you need distance from what drains you Sensory — when everything feels too loud, too bright, too much Creative — when you need to receive, not produce Spiritual — when you feel disconnected from meaning or belonging Environmental — when your space feels heavy, cluttered, or tense So many of us are trying to fix the wrong kind of tired. Trying to sleep through emotional exhaustion. Trying to push through spiritual depletion. Trying to stay productive through nervous system overwhelm. That’s why it still feels like… something isn’t landing. In my work as a Rest Guide, I see this all the time people bracing in one area while trying to heal another. That’s where the unlearning begins. I created a Rest Audit to help you understand what kind of rest your body is actually asking for right now. Not what you’ve been told you need but what you truly need. Your permission to rest differently is waiting.
